Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 6). Targeted pass over Ch. 4 (cross-cutting CHP Tables 8-10, CCS Table 11), Ch. 5 (per-product consumption, emission, BAT and IT tables for nitric acid, ammonia/urea, steam cracking, FCC propylene, acrylonitrile, hydrogen, methanol, adipic acid, soda ash, aromatics, carbon black, chlor-alkali, EO/MEG, EDC/VCM, PVC, PVC recycling, ethylbenzene/styrene) and Table 95 (new-plant investment costs, EUR 2013). Main file: SEC by carrier, process/combustion emissions as used in the study (electricity- and steam-production emissions, which the study counts, are in _other-values), IPCC default factors as separate contexts, whole-technology capex with reference capacity, CCS capture rates and costs, CHP parameters and Table 9 costs. Retrofit BAT/IT investment costs with a measurable host (N2O abatement, chlor-alkali conversions, ODC, aromatics heat integration, CCS) are loaded as capex COST BASIS incremental; the remaining BAT rows (percent savings with investment per t or per reference plant) are in _measures. Price years: BAT/IT table costs and Table 95 are EUR 2013 (Sect. 4.4 says all investment costs were escalated to 2013 with CEPCI; the BAT table headers print EUR only); text costs keep their printed years. Where the report itself assumed a year (BREF figures taken as 2006) this is noted. Model results (Ch. 8) not extracted. Energy: the report uses LHV for its own fuel conversions (Table 6) and labels only Table 26 / EFMA ammonia figures as LHV; most SEC rows are reprints (IEA 2009b, EC BREFs, Serpec-cc) with basis not stated.

(1) Table 28 and Table 43 list production costs (Holbrook and Leighty: average cost of ammonia USD 215/t; SSAS USD 145-445/t; biomass H2 EUR 2.3/kg) in the Investment cost column; loaded as cost-levelized from the text. (2) Table 27 urea row is under a per-t-NH3 header. (3) Table 9 row grouping is by layout only (Serpec 25-50 and <25 MW read as gas turbine); EPA ranges printed high-low. (4) Table 95 data-origin column spans several rows (nitric to urea, hydrogen/methanol, EB/styrene) so attribution is ambiguous. (5) Table 63 averages 0.211 and 6.152 carry footnote markers (read 0.21 and 6.15). (6) SCT-CPO capex for ammonia (EUR 835 million for 500 kt/y) is about five times the Table 95 ammonia plant cost. (7) Naphtha cracker total 12 GJ/t ethylene (study value) is net of by-product fuels and well below the 26-31 GJ/t in Table 34. (8) Text says "300-500 kt/d" typical ammonia plant size (should be t/d). (9) Steam-reforming H2 efficiency and electrolyser efficiencies mix HHV and LHV bases as printed.
